summary_html: A **judge orders** CPS to investigate or assess during civil/criminal proceedings. Federal funding statutes (ASFA/IV-E) tether court findings to child-welfare actions, embedding judicial oversight into intake-to-case flow.
authority_html:

- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — funding structure linking court oversight to agency actions

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court held that a juvenile court exceeds its jurisdiction if it transfers legal custody of a child from a parent to the county department at a pre-adjudicatory shelter hearing; at that stage the court may only continue shelter or release the child, and a temporary protective custody order reaches physical custody only.
key_cases.relevance: It defines exactly what a juvenile court may and may not order before adjudication when a case is opened on referral.
key_cases.quote: We will not infer from statutory silence a jurisdictional grant to a juvenile court to sever legal custody from a natural parent at a pre-adjudicatory shelter hearing.

key_cases.holding: The court held that the juvenile court had jurisdiction under the Children's Code to take the case at a shelter hearing and to issue temporary orders providing for the medical treatment of a gravely injured child whose parents were unable and unavailable to act, and that its order was proper.
key_cases.relevance: The case shows the juvenile court exercising jurisdiction and ordering protective and medical measures at the outset of a child-protection matter.
key_cases.quote: We hold, therefore, that the court had jurisdiction and its action was proper.

Social workers and workers in any facility or agency licensed or certified by the state
Commercial film and photographic print processors
Clergy members (not for information learned in a communication privileged under Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-90-107(1)(c))
Workers in the state department of human services
Officers and agents of the state bureau of animal protection, and animal control officers
Educators providing services through the federal WIC program
Directors, coaches, assistant coaches, and athletic program personnel employed by a private sports organization or program
Registered psychologist, marriage and family therapist, and licensed professional counselor candidates
Officials and employees of a county department of health or of human or social services
